title: RSpec Advanced
intro: RSpec is the dominant testing framework in the Rails ecosystem, and interviews at Rails companies test it specifically — not just generic testing concepts. The two most important RSpec-specific questions are the let vs let! distinction (let is lazy and memoised; let! is eager and runs before the example) and shared examples for DRY contract testing. This page covers the full RSpec toolkit at the intermediate level: shared_examples_for and it_behaves_like, shared_context with include_context, custom matchers with RSpec::Matchers.define, aggregate_failures for multiple assertions without early exit, have_enqueued_job and have_enqueued_mail for async assertions, and the Rails integration setup — the difference between spec_helper.rb and rails_helper.rb and when to use each.
